title: UK Space Agency - Operational Support to the International Charter: Space and Major Disasters
description:
The International Charter: Space and Major Disasters (“the Charter”) is a global agreement which aims to provide a unified system of space data acquisition and delivery to those affected by natural or man-made disasters. It provides and enables transmission of earth observation satellite data and pre-authorised resilience/emergency response bodies in response to “activations”. 
Further details on the Charter can be found at https://disasterscharter.org/
Unlike many space faring nations in the Charter, the UK Government does not own or operate its own national EO satellite system assets. The UK Government therefore fulfils its Charter commitments through partnership with the UK EO commercial sector. This procurement seeks to maintain and strengthen that model by securing operational support from an organisation with UK licensed and operated EO satellite data assets that can be contributed to Charter activations. 
The continued participation of UK EO commercial satellite operators in the Charter delivers both public benefit and strategic value by showcasing sovereign EO capabilities, supporting international disaster response and demonstrating operational utility of UK-developed EO missions.

original.description: ANUBIS (Asteroid NUdging By Ion-beam Shepherding) is a potential future Planetary Defence Cornerstone aiming to demonstrate the "ion beam shepherd" concept, which makes use of ion thrusters to deflect asteroids. The concept is of great interest to Planetary Defence and the scientific community, as demonstrated by various assessments, and in particular highlighted by the UN Space Mission Planning Advisory Group (SMPAG). The concept is one of the most promising candidates for deflecting potentially hazardous asteroids, when there is time enough to apply this technology.

original.description: The objective of the activity is to define and develop a free space optical communication testbed suitable for testing a cross-atmospheric optical connectivity in the horizontal link between Tallinn and Helsinki. Targeted Improvements: To create a terrestrial testbed capability allowing for demonstration and long-term communication testing. The testbed will provide information on the long-distance atmospheric channel and the stability of the optical links in fixed and mobile configuration. The testbed facility will support new technology developments for optical and quantum satellite communication. Description: Most of satellite constellations developed these days include intersatellite links. However, the adaptation of cross-atmospheric links remains to be progressing slowly. One of the challenges is the limited availability of outdoor, free-space testbeds. The proposed testbed facility will enable testing over the long-distance, cross-atmospheric channel created between two stations located in Tallinn and Helsinki. The testbed will allow for fixed-points free-space optical connection, demonstrating and validating a continuous datalink between interoperable terminals and transceivers aligned with satellite optical communication standards. The testbed should allow to collect and analyse information on the atmospheric channel over multiple seasons. It should monitor weather conditions and investigate beam dissipation dynamics and various mitigation strategies. The spatially dynamic optical links will also be demonstrated to test and validate a free-space optical datalink between moving terminals. The testbed should foresee and facilitate testing of quantum-encrypted free-space optical communication capabilities. The preparation to demonstrate data-relay with a satellite link is planned to be included in the activity.

original.description: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) safeguards system is designed to verify States' legal undertakings to use nuclear material for exclusively peaceful purposes. States declare their nuclear material and activities to the IAEA, and the IAEA verifies thecorrectness and completeness of these declarations.This requires robust and resilient GNSS trackers which can withstand sophisticated attacks (jamming, spoofing, and especially treacherous meaconing) and tampering attempts by State-level actors, providing Assured PNT (Trusted positioning data).The GNSS tracker shall be battery powered and capable of unsupervised operations. In previous projects (in particular, EL1-077) building blocks for this technology have been developed. The IAEA has expressed interest in a joint project to increase the protection against additional attacks identified and to raise the TRL level and to make the tracker ready forcommercialization. The objective of the activity is to study, design, implement and demonstrate a resilient and robust GNSS tracker to support IAEA safeguards activities, and other similar activities requiring Assured PNTThe tasks to be performed shall include:Based on EL1-077, the activity will study, design, implement and demonstrate the technologies required for the GNSS tracker, capable of detecting and mitigating jamming, meaconing and spoofing attacks, with focus on concrete uses cases and attack scenarios identified by IAEA.Additional technologies (for example tightly coupled INS and CRPAs) will be integrated into a functional prototype. As part of the demonstration, the prototype will be subject to thorough tests representative of challenging jamming, meaconing and spoofing scenarios mounted by capable attackers.The activity is part of a roadmap to make available to customers GNSS trackers with Assured PNT and will bring the technology to a TRL which will allow industry to make confident proposals for an Element 2. The activity will not include any Galileo PRS technology, as per NAVISP Declaration.

original.description: Objective: To develop a proof-of-concept of a modular robust waveform for E2E communications that offers further protection for the missions, in a modular approach in accordance with the mission security needs.Description:Intentional RF interference is a threat to space missions, as it can disrupt the radio links between satellite and ground/users. There are waveform techniques that can counter or mitigate the impact of that interference but they need to be designed specifically against reference threats. This activity is aimed at developing a modular robust waveform for end-to-end (E2E) communications offering further protection for the missions, by designing the waveform aspects as well as the receiver operations. It will consider typical RF threats and tune the waveform against the most common ones, so that space missions do not have to develop new solutions for their case. The design of the modular robust waveform can include cryptographically robust spread sequences that can be used to drive a frequency hopping scheme, or a direct Sequence spread spectrum modulation, coupled with Adaptive Coding and Modulation (ACM). The adaptation algorithm of the ACM can cover both the typical Modulation and Coding schemes as well as the Transmission Security (TRANSEC) functions (e.g. Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum and Frequency Hopping), providing flexible level of protection based on the link conditions. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Consolidation of the most common RF interference signals and attacks method - Investigation of state of theart signal techniques to counter RF interference and development of a SWAT analysis to select the optimum measures for the consolidated attacks options. - Detailed design of the waveform blocks to counter the identified common RF interference threats. Particular emphasis shall be devoted to the Add-on modularity so that each block can be added as plug-in. - Development of a Proof of Concept simulator including signal generator/receiver of the waveform and assessment of the E2E performance of the proposed Waveform. - Investigation of the regulatory constraints from the Radio Frequency Compatibility with specific focus on the impact of wideband signals on ITU frequency bands allocation. The software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community License, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member States can access to it and can provide update to the community of users.Deliverables: Report, Software
